title: Shortest distances with negative edges
description:
Every edge of a weighted, directed graph has an integer length, and some lengths are negative. The distance from one vertex to another is the smallest total length of any path from the first to the second. A negative cycle is a cycle whose lengths add up to less than zero: going around it again always makes a path shorter, so vertices past it have no shortest distance at all.

Implement a struct type called Edge with three integer fields: From, the vertex the edge leaves; To, the vertex it enters; and Weight, its length. Then implement a function called BellmanFord that receives the number of vertices, a list of edges, and a source vertex, and returns two values: a list holding, for each vertex, its distance from the source, and a boolean that is true when the distances are valid. Vertices are numbered from zero.

With the edges 0->1 (length 5), 1->2 (1), 1->3 (2), 2->4 (1), 4->3 (-1) and source 0:
BellmanFord(5, edges, 0) -> [0, 5, 6, 6, 7], true. Vertex 3 is reached through 1, 2 and 4 for 5 + 1 + 1 - 1 = 6, which beats the direct route through 1 for 7.

If a negative cycle can be reached from the source, return no list and false. With the edges 0->1 (4), 1->2 (-6), 2->3 (5), 3->1 (-2), the cycle 1->2->3->1 adds up to -3:
BellmanFord(4, edges, 0) -> nothing, false.

A vertex that cannot be reached from the source gets the largest value an integer can hold, since -1 is now a real distance. A negative cycle that the source cannot reach does not count: with the edges 0->1 (2), 2->3 (1), 3->2 (-3):
BellmanFord(4, edges, 0) -> [0, 2, largest integer, largest integer], true.

The hidden tests also check that edges only go one way, a negative edge that is not part of any cycle, a cycle whose lengths add up to exactly zero (not negative), a single edge from a vertex back to itself with a negative length, and edges listed in the worst possible order, so that the shortest distances only settle after the maximum number of rounds.
objective: Recall Bellman-Ford: relax every edge once per vertex minus one, then run one more pass in which any edge that still relaxes proves a reachable negative cycle, never relaxing out of an unreached vertex.
